## Getting Started

### Download and install GRASS

Install GRASS 8.4 or newer for your platform from the
[GRASS download page](https://grass.osgeo.org/download/). The workflows on this
site also use GRASS addons, which are installed with `g.extension` as
needed by the scripts and notebooks.

### Create Python Virtual Environment

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
```

### Activate Python Virtual Environment

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

### Install Python Dependencies

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

```

### Setup GRASS Projects

Now create a new GRASS project for each of the study areas. The metadata for
each site is stored in `site-CRS-info.txt` at the repository root:

| Site | State | EPSG | Resolution (m) | NAIP Year | Latitude | Longitude |
|------|-------|------|---------------:|-----------|---------:|----------:|
| clay-center | Kansas | 32614 | 3 | 2021 | 39.4003765 | -97.0630433 |
| coweeta | North Carolina | 26917 | 10 | 2022 | 35.0467816 | -83.4497516 |
| SFREC | California | 26910 | 1 | 2022 | 39.2731237 | -121.3103158 |
| SJER | California | 26911 | 1 | 2022 | 37.0949164 | -119.7447120 |
| tx069-playas | Texas | 32613 | 8 | 2022 | 34.4884740 | -102.1068130 |

Download and import the site data:

```bash
python3 scripts/download_data.py
```
